newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian telecom, postal employees return to work.
newsitem.headline: Indian telecom, postal employees return to work.

text.p: Some one million Indian telecommunication and postal workers were back at work on Wednesday at the end of a week-long strike after the government agreed to lift a ceiling on bonus payments, their leaders said.
"Our demand has been conceded. Therefore, the strike ended," O.P. Gupta, head of The National Federation of Telecom Employees, told Reuters on Wednesday.
Telecommunications Minister Beni Prasad Varma announced on Tuesday the cabinet decision on payments, reversing the austerity measure imposed by the government earlier this year.
A government statement said on Tuesday employees would be paid a productivity-linked bonus.
The strike started on October 23 in protest at a decision to impose a 3,500-rupee ($100) ceiling on annual pay bonuses.
Workers argued that a bonus ceiling for railway workers had already been lifted, setting a precedent for other state sector employees.
"Our struggle was against the disparity between the payment of bonus to the railway and telecom employees. We have achieved that," Gupta said.
The strike crippled government postal services, with millions of letters piling up in post offices across India.
Telecommunications services, largely automated, were not hit severely but operator-related services, and repair and maintenance services were disrupted.
